verdict.reason: Verified independently. `moveCells` (sheet.ts:1465-1519) validates only `isMergeSplitByMove` (1478-1483) and then relocates every fully-contained merged block via `moveMergeMap` at line 1516; there is no `crossesFreezePane` call in `moveCells` or in the public wrappers `moveRows`/`moveColumns` (sheet.ts:1279-1288). The invariant the PR enforces lives at `crossesFreezePane` (sheet.ts:2500-2510) and is applied only at `planPasteMerges` (2430, `merge-paste-frozen`) and `moveRangeTo` (2685-2695, `merge-move-frozen`), whose own comment (2680-2684) says a straddling block is not drawable by the renderer. The bypass is reachable from the UI: the drag-reorder drop handler calls `moveRows`/`moveColumns` at view/worksheet.ts:4658-4659 with only a same-position check (4649-4654), and `computeDropIndex` (4606-4625) resolves drops inside the frozen pane. Walking the reviewer's example through `isMergeSplitByMove` (merging.ts:181-195, `fullyInside` → false) and `moveMergeMap` (merging.ts:161-176) yields a block at rows 2-3 with frozenRows=2, which `crossesFreezePane` would reject. The comment at worksheet-structure.ts:271-272 concerns freeze counts, not merge placement, so it is not a guard. This is a new guard with another entry point reaching the protected state — in lane and blocking at major.

finding.evidence: `copyBuffer = undefined` now only happens in `clearCopyBuffer` (sheet.ts:2141, reached solely from the Escape keybinding at packages/sheets/src/view/worksheet.ts:5118) and on a consumed cut (sheet.ts:2286). Nothing in `insertRows`/`deleteRows` (`shiftMergeMap`, sheet.ts:1327) or `moveCells` (sheet.ts:1516) shifts or drops `copyBuffer.sourceRange` / `copyBuffer.merges`. After copy → insert rows → Ctrl+V (clipboard text unchanged), `paste` still takes the internal branch and computes `deltaRow/deltaCol` (sheet.ts:2250) and `planPasteMerges`' destination range from a source range that no longer describes the data, mis-relocating formulas and applying a stale merge layout. verdict.reason: Every claimed location checks out. `copyBuffer` is reset only at sheet.ts:2141 (clearCopyBuffer) and sheet.ts:2286 (consumed cut); a repo-wide grep finds no other reset. clearCopyBuffer has exactly one production caller, the Escape keybinding at view/worksheet.ts:5117-5119. Both paste paths (view/worksheet.ts:4941-4947, view/spreadsheet.ts:724-728) now explicitly do not clear the buffer. The structural mutators shift/remap every other piece of positional state — rangeStyles, conditionalFormats, dataValidations, merges (sheet.ts:1327, sheet.ts:1516), activeCell, ranges — but never copyBuffer, so nothing invalidates or shifts copyBuffer.sourceRange/merges after insertRows/deleteRows/moveRows. The stale buffer is reachable: paste takes the internal branch on unchanged clipboard text (sheet.ts:2243) and computes deltaRow/deltaCol plus planPasteMerges' destination from the stale sourceRange (sheet.ts:2250-2265), and the overlay re-renders getCopyRange() every frame (view/worksheet.ts:5600). This is the blast-radius lane: a view-side change extended the lifetime of model state that the model's own structural operations do not maintain, and a second consumer (the overlay) reads it. Impact magnitude is partly arguable (stale grid and stale sourceRange cancel for references below an insertion seam), but straddling references, the persistent stale marquee, and the copy-time merge snapshot applied over an unbounded window are real, so the finding stands.

mergedFrom.summary: `setFreezePane` can create a straddling merge that the new guard forbids elsewhere

finding.summary: Drag-move (`moveRangeTo`) bypasses the new freeze-pane merge guard
finding.evidence: The delta establishes the invariant "a merged block may not straddle a freeze boundary" and enforces it for internal paste via `crossesFreezePane` (sheet.ts:2418-2424, refusal `merge-paste-frozen`). `moveRangeTo` re-creates the moved blocks at the destination with no such check: packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:2749-2755 does `await this.store.setMerge(anchor, merge.span)` after only the `merge-source-split` / `merge-dest-partial` pre-flights (2658-2670). Reachable from the UI drag-move at packages/sheets/src/view/worksheet.ts:4350 (`await sheet.moveRangeTo(sourceRange, target)`) — dragging a merged block from the scrolling body into/over the frozen pane produces exactly the block the paste path now refuses, which the renderer (view/gridcanvas.ts pane painting, layout.ts:234-250) assumes cannot exist. Fix belongs in `moveRangeTo`: run the same `crossesFreezePane` check on the translated blocks and refuse with `merge-paste-frozen` (or a move-specific reason).

verdict.reason: The finding claims `moveRangeTo` re-creates moved blocks at the destination with no freeze-boundary check. The code does not read that way: sheet.ts:2685-2695 applies `crossesFreezePane` to each moved block's *translated* range (deltaRow/deltaCol applied) and returns early with `this.refuse('merge-move-frozen')`. That guard sits after the `merge-source-split` (2668) and `merge-dest-partial` (2676) pre-flights and before any mutation — `fetchGrid` (2697), `store.beginBatch()` (2712), and the merge re-creation `await this.store.setMerge(anchor, merge.span)` (2779). The finding's cited mutation lines 2749-2755 are the source-cell clearing loop, not setMerge. `merge-move-frozen` is a declared refusal (sheet.ts:233) and is handled in the view (view/worksheet.ts:114), so the UI drag-move caller (view/worksheet.ts:4352) surfaces it. Tests confirm the behaviour in both directions: merge.test.ts:690-718 (straddling drop refused, source block intact) and merge.test.ts:720-739 (same-side move allowed). The prescribed fix is already implemented at the exact location named.

mergedFrom.summary: A refused `merge-paste-partial` paste still loses the user's cut/copy buffer, because the view clears it unconditionally after `paste()` returns

finding.summary: Both view paste paths call `clearCopyBuffer()` unconditionally right after `sheet.paste(...)`, so the new merge propagation only ever runs on the FIRST paste after a copy
finding.evidence: packages/sheets/src/view/worksheet.ts:4937-4938 `await this.sheet!.paste({ text, html }); this.sheet!.clearCopyBuffer();` and packages/sheets/src/view/spreadsheet.ts:724-725 do the same. `Sheet.paste` only takes the internal branch when `this.copyBuffer && text === this.copyBuffer.text` (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:2233). Once the view has cleared the buffer, a second Ctrl+V of the same clipboard content falls through to the plain-TSV branch (sheet.ts:2290), which carries no merges and is explicitly exempt from the new plan/refuse logic. The user-visible consequence is precisely the bug this change fixes: the 2nd and later pastes re-introduce the 'values written into cells hidden under a destination merge, resurfacing on unmerge' behaviour, and `merge-paste-partial` never fires. The new unit tests drive `Sheet` directly and never call `clearCopyBuffer`, so nothing in the suite covers the real app sequence. Fix likely belongs at the two view call sites (only clear on cut, or clear only when the paste actually consumed the buffer).

verdict.reason: The described code is not present. Neither view paste path calls `clearCopyBuffer()` after `sheet.paste(...)`. `packages/sheets/src/view/worksheet.ts:4941-4948` contains an explicit comment that the buffer is deliberately NOT cleared, followed by `await this.sheet!.paste({ text, html }); this.render();`. `packages/sheets/src/view/spreadsheet.ts:724-730` is the same: comment plus `await this.sheet.paste({ text, html }); this.worksheet.render(); this.notifySelectionChange();`. The reviewer's cited lines 4937-4938 are actually the `navigator.clipboard.readText()` fallback branch. A repo-wide grep for `clearCopyBuffer` yields exactly one call site in src: `packages/sheets/src/view/worksheet.ts:5118`, inside the Escape key handler guarded by `if (this.sheet!.getCopyRange())` — not a paste path. Because the copy buffer is never cleared by pasting, the internal merge-aware branch at `sheet.ts:2233` (`this.copyBuffer && text === this.copyBuffer.text`) remains reachable on the 2nd and later pastes, so the claimed consequence (repeat pastes degrade to the plain-TSV branch, merge propagation runs only once, `merge-paste-partial` never fires) has no basis in this tree.
